pairs.difference: B: the gold mirror frame is lit almost evenly from the front. The scrolls have only thin soft dark lines, with no shadow side down the frame, and a weak, pale cast shadow sits on the stone to the left. Light bias is 0.132, below the real floor. A: the glass has a clear lit left wall and darker base, plus a tight contact shadow with a coloured glow on the table. Its form contrast is also low (0.312), but the transparent subject explains that, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Light the mirror from the upper right. Make the left side of the gold frame clearly darker, with soft deep shadow under each scroll, and put a darker tight shadow where the feet touch the stone.

pairs.difference: B: the binocular barrels go nearly white on top against near-black eyecups, with a long heavy cast shadow to the lower right and a darkened top edge on the floor. This reads as hard photographic light, and shading range 0.925 is above the real ceiling. A: the rocking horse has gentle top-left modelling on the body and legs and a soft dark shadow under the rockers, inside the real ranges.
pairs.fix: Soften the light on the binoculars. Use a broad soft sheen along the barrels instead of near-white tops, open up the shadow side, and make the cast shadow shorter, softer and lighter.

pairs.difference: B: the fan is nearly flat. The pleats differ by paint rather than by light, the wooden sticks have no real shadow side, and there is only a thin edge darkening instead of a cast shadow on the backdrop. Form contrast 0.213 and light bias 0.09 are both below the real floor. A: the spider's round abdomen turns from a soft top sheen into a dark underside, and its legs have a lit top and shaded underside, though its light bias is also low.
pairs.fix: Light the fan from the upper left. Make each pleat turn from a bright crest into a dark valley, shade the lower-right edge of the sticks, and add a soft shadow behind the fan.

pairs.difference: B: the log cabin is lit flat from the front. The wall, door and log ends share nearly the same brightness, the deep roof overhang drops only a thin shadow on the wall, and the ground has almost no cast shadow. Light bias 0.161 is below the real floor. A: the pool bar has a clear shadow under the thatch, a counter that turns from a lit top to a darker side, and stools with lit tops and dark stems.
pairs.fix: Bring the sun in from the upper left. Drop a wide soft shadow from the roof onto the front wall, shade the right side of each log end, and cast a clear shadow from the cabin across the grass.

pairs.difference: A: the gate's stone piers are even from left to right and the iron bars have no light side. The bars cast no shadow on the path. The only local light is an orange patch at each lantern. Shading range 0.494 and light bias 0.035 are far below real. B: the pool bar has a shared direction across thatch, counter and stools, and its shadows fall under the roof and on the water.
pairs.fix: Set one clear light direction from the moon at the upper right. Give the piers a lit right face and darker left face, put a pale edge on the bars, and cast long soft bar shadows across the path.

pairs.difference: A: the spotlight's dark barrel has a smooth turn, a broad sheen and a tinted rim, with form contrast and light bias only slightly above the real ceiling. B: the fuel pump has a light cap and a darker left side, within all real ranges, but only a faint shadow on its base despite the low sun in the background. Neither shows a clear lighting tell.

A: the candy corn is a soft glowing blob. Light barely turns across the cone, with only a faint darkening at the edges and no real core shadow, so the bands read through colour alone. Shading range 0.518 and form contrast 0.329 are below the real floor. Its strong purple cast shadow is the only firm shape. B: the fruit plate has crisp droplets, shaded undersides on the fruit and a clear plate shadow, within the real ranges.
pairs.fix: Light the candy corn from the upper left. Give the cone a clear bright side and a darker right side with a soft core shadow, plus one soft sheen on the upper left.

pairs.difference: A: the moon has no terminator. The disc stays nearly even from edge to edge with only slight darkening at the bottom, the craters are shallow, and it reads as a flat plate rather than a ball. Form contrast 0.252 is below the real floor. B: the bugle's bell turns strongly from a bright lip to a dark throat, with long highlights along the tube, within the real range.
pairs.fix: Light the moon as a sphere from the upper left. Let it fall to a deep shadow along the lower right, and give each crater a dark inner wall on the lit side and a bright opposite rim.

pairs.difference: A: the red armchair's front faces stay fairly close in brightness, with low contrast across the backrest and seat. Only the wing edges and underside fall dark. Form contrast 0.276 and light bias 0.144 are below the real floor. B: the locker has bright edges, a clear interior shadow and a wall shadow to the left. Its own pale rim is rather pillowy and its light bias of 0.2 is also just low, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Light the armchair from the upper left. Make the right side of the backrest and arm clearly darker, deepen the shadow under the seat cushion and arm rolls, and put a soft sheen on the left wing.

pairs.difference: A: the street lamp's dark iron has abrupt jumps from pale sheen on the dome and arm to near-black, while the glass stays flat around the bulb. Form contrast 0.68 is above the real ceiling. B: the feeder has gentler plank shading, a clear dark interior and a soft shadow under the roof, inside the real ranges.
pairs.fix: Soften the lamp's metal. Use a broad low sheen on the dome and arm instead of pale bands, lift the shadow side slightly, and let the bulb's glow brighten the glass around it.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers are lit frontally across uppers and soles, while a long hard shadow runs left as if from a separate light. The form and the cast shadow do not agree. Light bias 0.019 is far below the real floor and range 0.82 is above the ceiling. B: the candle has a warm top glow falling off down the wax, a soft shaded side, and a saucer shadow to the left that fits its form.
pairs.fix: Light the shoes from the upper right to match the shadow. Make their right sides bright and their left sides fall into soft shade, then shorten and soften the cast shadow.

pairs.difference: A: the lantern is hard-lit, with a pale top on the roof against near-black under-edges, sharp white streaks on the glass, and a base that falls straight to black with no bounce. Range 0.855 and contrast 0.663 are above the real ceiling. B: the blue neck pillow turns gently from a soft top light into shade at the lower ends, with puckers modelled softly, inside the real ranges.
pairs.fix: Use softer light on the lantern. Make a broad gentle sheen on the roof, narrower and fainter streaks on the glass, and add soft green bounce from the flame and backdrop on the dark underside.

pattern: Generated cards break from the real ones in two opposite ways. Most often they are lit flat from the front: side planes barely darken, there is no clear core shadow, and spheres and cones read as discs (moon, candy corn, fan, cabin, gate). Cast shadows are missing or disagree with the form shading, as on the sneakers. Others overshoot into hard light, with near-white tops, near-black undersides and no bounce (binoculars, lantern). Real cards keep one clear direction, a shadow side that goes well down but stays open, a soft turn into it, and tight contact shadows. In the lessons, the lens on generated cards also tends to stay warm and even, while real cards show a cooler, deeper shadow side. Confidence is limited: the p01, p02, p09, p10 and p12 calls are weak and rely partly on measured numbers, and p06 gave no reason to choose.
